items.title: Designing inclusive interactive oral assessments: Practical learnings for educators
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence continues to impact the higher education sector, Interactive Oral Assessments (IOAs) are increasingly used to assure assessment integrity. Whilst there are IOA best practice guidelines, there are concerns that the pace of implementation has compromised design, and considerations regarding student preparation, equity and inclusivity are being overlooked. This concise paper considers these issues through a case study of a postgraduate business subject and provides practical advice for how student preparation for oral tasks can be embedded within a curriculum without detracting from disciplinary knowledge and content. The design addressed five areas to support student IOA preparation: creating authentic scenarios; designing inclusive assessment practices for diverse cohorts; structured student preparation; balancing IOA preparation with course content coverage; and ensuring alignment between preparation activities and the actual IOA experience. Student feedback and educator observations suggest students felt increasingly prepared and supported throughout the semester. Recommendations are made for educators considering IOA including incorporation of low-stakes practice, creating classroom safety, setting clear expectations, preparing exemplars, focusing on student and educator preparation, and collaborating with others. This paper extends existing IOA literature by addressing inclusive practices for increasingly diverse student cohorts and contributes practical strategies for educators seeking to design IOA’s that support inclusion while balancing curriculum time and disciplinary content requirements.

items.title: Designing psychiatric environments tailored to the needs of geriatric patients: spatial solutions in geriatric hospital wards that reduce stress and dissorientation
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The progressive aging of the population increases the demand for specialized psychiatric wards adapted to the needs of older adults. A particular challenge is designing spaces for patients with dementia, as environmental changes may cause disorientation, deterioration of mental condition, and increased behavioral disturbances. Properly designed therapeutic environments improve safety, support spatial orientation, and enhance psychological comfort. The aim of this study was to identify and analyze good design practices in geriatric psychiatric wards based on the principles of health-promoting architecture. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted, covering publications on healthcare architecture, environmental psychiatry, and therapeutic environment design, with particular focus on patients with dementia. Current guidelines, design recommendations, and practical solutions used in healthcare facilities were also analyzed. The study had a descriptive and comparative character. Identified architectural solutions were assessed using a qualitative comparative approach according to criteria related to health-promoting architecture, including spatial orientation, accessibility, environmental safety, sensory comfort, social interaction, and reduction of stress and behavioral symptoms. RESULTS: The analysis showed that clear functional layouts, spatial zoning, and intuitive wayfinding reduce disorientation and improve patient independence. Important elements include appropriate colors, visual identification features, natural lighting, contact with nature, and ergonomic and safe equipment. Communal spaces support social interaction, reduce isolation, and enhance therapeutic processes. These solutions may reduce stress, aggressive behaviors, and improve quality of care. CONCLUSIONS: Designing geriatric psychiatric wards according to the needs of people with dementia supports treatment effectiveness and user safety. Integration of architectural knowledge with psychiatry and environmental psychology enables the creation of health-promoting environments. The findings may support modernization of existing wards and the design of new facilities, while indicating the need for further research on the impact of therapeutic environments on clinical outcomes and patient well-being in long-term psychiatric care settings for older adults. items.title: Differentiating Agricultural Tractor Brands and Models through User-Reported Quality Profiles
items.abstract: User experience with agricultural tractors is multidimensional and can be obscured by a single brand-level score. This study analysed 140 tractor-evaluation questionnaires covering 21 tractor brands and 44 detailed quality attributes rated on a seven-point scale. Descriptive analyses used the complete sample, whereas formal brand differentiation was restricted to six brands represented by at least five questionnaires (N = 108). Attribute-wise differences were evaluated by the Kruskal–Wallis test, epsilon-squared effect sizes, Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction, and stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. To test whether the 44-attribute profiles contained reproducible brand information beyond univariate contrasts, a shrinkage linear discriminant model was evaluated by stratified five-fold cross-validation and a label-permutation test. Spare-parts availability (6.26), engine reliability (6.16), and forward visibility (6.14) were the highest-rated attributes, whereas storage availability (4.64), passenger space (4.89), and vibration damping (4.94) were lowest. The strongest brand differentiation occurred for ease of radiator cleaning (ε² = 0.508), vibration damping (0.499), overall comfort (0.460), rear hydraulic-coupler access (0.448), and cab lighting (0.440). Cross-validated balanced brand-classification accuracy reached 0.371, compared with a six-class chance level of 0.167 (permutation p = 0.002). At model level, within-brand centering separated model-specific domain profiles from the corresponding brand baseline; 12 models represented by at least three users were visualized. The results show that practical tractor quality is structured by specific ergonomic, maintainability, reliability, and ownership attributes and that these detailed profiles contain reproducible information at both brand and model levels.
